category_title: Adolescents with confrontational behaviors and externalizing family stress
minimal_context: James is asked to join a group of peers to complete a shared assignment in his secondary school classroom.
dialogue:
TUTOR: James, it's time for group work. Please sit with your assigned peers and share the materials for this assignment.

STUDENT: I'm not sitting with them. They keep looking at me like I'm going to nick their stuff. Like, twenty quid doesn't just go randomly missing and you forget about it, that's what they're all thinking about my family.

TUTOR: Nobody is saying that. Just join the group and start the activity.

STUDENT: Yeah, right. It's always about my sister. So I don’t know what’s going on, if she’s had second thoughts about it or if she’s put it anonymous no, questions asked or that... but everyone in here treats me like I'm the one doing it.

TUTOR: We need to get this work done, James. Please just sit down and cooperate with your classmates.

STUDENT: (Pushes the desk aggressively and stands up) I said I'm not doing it! You all think I'm just like her! 'Why can't you just be good?', right? That's what you want to say! I have always thought twice … like not just gone in on the first thought that I’ve had, but I'm sick of everyone judging me!

options.A: Send a clear message to the student regarding dissatisfaction with his behavior.
options.B: Explicitly incorporate elements that promote self-compassion into the immediate response.
options.C: Tell the student to leave the classroom immediately or call the police.
options.D: Provide detailed instructions for each specific element of the shared group assignment.
